\chapter{One Exchange, Two Figures}
\label{ch:mw-numbered-exchange}
\hlchaptermodality{36}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can run a six-turn counter exchange in which both sides name an amount, at a shop, a food stall, and a rickshaw.}

The twelve numbers and ten figures are retrieved at a distance, run over the shopping, food, and transport words in turn, and the five-turn exchange of chapter 31 is then re-run with the seller's figure and the buyer's offer in it.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Practice]{The whole count, at a distance}

\label{lesson:MW-R36-count-at-distance}



\begin{quote}
Say the bargaining request, recall the five-number payoff from four chapters back, then write \textbf{\mw{ए}}.

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Recall:} \textbf{\mw{७}} and \textbf{\mw{८}}, and which Latin figure each is mistaken for
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Everything, shuffled, with no chapter to give the answer away.

\begin{enumerate}
\raggedright
  \item Hear twelve amounts named singly and out of order; say each back.
  \item Read twelve printed figures and say each as a word.
  \item Write six amounts from dictation in words and six in figures, the choice named only as you write.
  \item Say the three that rhyme, the two that end in the tens \textbf{\mw{स}}, and the four figures a Latin eye reads wrongly.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}; \href{https://www.omniglot.com/language/numbers/rajasthani.htm}{Omniglot, Numbers in Rajasthani}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{The shopping map, with prices on it}

\label{lesson:MW-R36-shopping-numbered}



\begin{quote}
Write the bargaining request, then recall the seven-word shopping payoff.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Take the seven shopping words one at a time. For each one:

\begin{enumerate}
\raggedright
  \item Ask its price with the question from chapter 27.
  \item Hear a figure back and say the amount aloud.
  \item Offer a lower figure with \textbf{\mw{करो।}}
  \item Write the seller's amount as a Devanagari figure and your own as a word.
\end{enumerate}

The word \textbf{\mw{भाव}} has meant price since chapter 18 and could not be answered until now. Say what changed.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{The food map, ordered and paid for}

\label{lesson:MW-R36-food-numbered}



\begin{quote}
Recall the seven-word food payoff, then write the bring request and the word that carries it.

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Recall:} \textbf{\mw{दस} \mw{करो।}}, and the chapter-28 request it replaced
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Take the seven food words one at a time.

\begin{enumerate}
\raggedright
  \item Order it with \textbf{\mw{लावो।}}
  \item Ask what it costs and hear a figure between \emph{ek} and \emph{das}.
  \item Say the amount, then hand over the money with the chapter-30 turn.
  \item Write the amount twice: once as a word, once as a figure.
\end{enumerate}

A stall prices tea at \emph{pāṅch} and a plate at \emph{das}. This is where the first five numbers stop being a recitation.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{The transport map, with a fare on it}

\label{lesson:MW-R36-transport-numbered}



\begin{quote}
Recall the five-word transport payoff and the four-skill bargaining payoff, then write bus.

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Recall:} \textbf{\mw{१००}} and \textbf{\mw{सो}}, and which of the two is longer
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Take the five transport words one at a time.

\begin{enumerate}
\raggedright
  \item Ask the fare with the price question.
  \item Hear a figure — a rickshaw across a town centre asks \emph{bīs} rather than \emph{pāṅch}.
  \item Offer a lower one with \textbf{\mw{करो।}}, and say the amount aloud twice so the driver hears the same figure you meant.
  \item Write both figures down, the asked and the offered.
\end{enumerate}

Say why this exchange has to be finished before the journey and not after it.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{The five least-drilled signs}

\label{lesson:MW-R36-letters-close}



\begin{quote}
Write the price question and the word for very, then recall the ticket payoff.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Five signs, alone, from spoken cues and with no word around them: \textbf{\mw{ए}}, \textbf{\mw{४}}, \textbf{\mw{५}}, \textbf{\mw{७}}, \textbf{\mw{८}}.

Then put each back to work once. \textbf{\mw{ए}} opens \textbf{\mw{एक}} and its mark rides over the second spelling of six; the four figures write four of this slice's twelve amounts. Write those six things and check each sign against the model only after writing it.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Payoff — one exchange, with an amount in it}

\label{lesson:MW-C36-numbered-exchange}



\begin{quote}
Run the five-turn counter exchange from chapter 31, say the take-it word, write the paying turn, and write \textbf{\mw{ए}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Six turns now, and two of them are numbers.

\begin{enumerate}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{\mw{ये} \mw{कपड़ा} \mw{दिखावो।}} — show me this cloth
  \item \textbf{\mw{ये} \mw{कितणे} \mw{कू} \mw{है}?} — how much is this?
  \item \textbf{\mw{बीस।}} — twenty
  \item \textbf{\mw{ये} \mw{घणो} \mw{महंगो} \mw{है।}} — this is very expensive
  \item \textbf{\mw{दस} \mw{करो।}} — make it ten
  \item \textbf{\mw{पैसा} \mw{ले} \mw{लो।}} — take the money
\end{enumerate}

Run it in four separately scored skills, over the shopping words, the food words and the transport words in turn, changing nothing but the noun and the two figures.

Turn 3 is what chapter 31 could not hear and turn 5 is what it could not say. Everything else on this list has been in the book since chapter 30.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}; \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}; \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-10-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 10}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Close the numeral slice}

\label{lesson:MW-R36-script-close}



\begin{quote}
Recall the six-turn payoff, write the take-it word, and write the bargaining request it now shares a chapter with.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Everything this slice added, from dictation, with no model in view.

\begin{enumerate}
\raggedright
  \item The letter: \textbf{\mw{ए}}, and the mark \textbf{\mw{े}} beside it.
  \item The twelve words, shuffled, from \textbf{\mw{एक}} to \textbf{\mw{सो}}.
  \item The ten figures, shuffled, from \textbf{\mw{०}} to \textbf{\mw{९}}.
  \item The two turns: \textbf{\mw{बीस।}} and \textbf{\mw{दस} \mw{करो।}}
\end{enumerate}

Repair only what missed. Then say what the whole slice cost the hand: one letter and ten figures, against twelve numbers and a bargaining turn that finally has a figure in it.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
